sights.w: NRHP-listed former ballpark where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his only Central Florida speech ("Integration Now", 6 March 1964) from the pitcher's mound; the city opened the Tinker Field History Plaza with a King bust and history markers in 2018 beside Camping World Stadium.

sights.w: Downtown's 1921 movie palace built by former mayor Braxton Beacham Sr. — vaudeville house, Great Southern Music Hall, and a string of nightclubs before reverting to its name in 2011; still a live-music/event venue on Orange Avenue.

sights.w: One of Orlando's oldest theaters (1963) — the city's first two-screen cinema, long a Rocky Horror haunt, now a concert hall owned by the Orlando Philharmonic; Orlando Weekly lists it among surviving historic landmarks and News 6 covered its $10M renovation award.

Tasty Chomps and WFTV feature it in their market guides.
